next_step: Confirm final capacity numbers + legal review; get internal perf sign-off or lose to competitor
notes:
Account summary: Late-stage procurement stalled; high technical interest but major throughput/capacity doubts during burst traffic windows. AE/SE ran a scoped POC in January — results mixed.

Key background: Eclipse Bay is a SaaS telemetry vendor that ingests telemetry events and runs real-time anomaly scoring and alerting. They have spiky traffic (release days, incident storms) where short-duration burst QPS can be 5-8x baseline. They need sub-100ms p50 on per-event scoring and predictable tail latency.

POC & technical timeline (bullets):
- 2025-11-12: Intro call (Aisha) — asked about per-tenant isolation and residency. Interested in Dedicated + VPC.
- 2025-12-02: Scoping workshop with SE (Tomás) — provided workload traces, typical burst factor ~6x for ~3-8 minutes.
- 2026-01-10: POC kickoff — synthetic replay of traces against hosted and dedicated test clusters.
- 2026-01-22: POC interim sync (ff-2026-01-29-ebb2 transcript) — initial observations: steady-state good, bursts caused queueing and KV cache thrash. SE recommended larger pool + autoscale policy + prefix caching.
- 2026-01-30: Load test 3 results — p95 latency spiked to 800-1,200ms under 6x burst; token throughput dropped due to queueing/backpressure.
- 2026-02-05: Cost review with finance — Dedicated sizing estimated at 2.5x their initial budget; questioned ROI.
- 2026-02-12: Procurement/legal sent SOC2 + KMS questions; engineering asked for latency SLA for bursts.
- 2026-02-16: Competitor demo (FastServe.ai) — competitor claimed elastic edge autoscaling and lower committed cost; customer began favoring them.
- 2026-02-20: AE follow-up — account dark; last activity today.

Customer concerns raised:
- "We cannot tolerate long queues during incident storms — alerts need to land within 2s." (VP Eng)
- Price vs committed Dedicated sizing — finance balked at 2.5x commit.
- Unclear team ownership after SRE reorg; no clear deployment champion.

SE notes & technical fit verdict:
- Root cause during POC: KV cache eviction and insufficient multi-tenant isolation on shared pools led to tail degradation under real burst patterns.
- Recommended mitigations: larger reserved GPU pool, aggressive prefix/KV caching, request-level admission control + warm standby nodes for burst windows, and targeted quantization for non-critical models.
- Risk: mitigations increase committed capacity/cost. Customer did not push for a second POC variant with those changes due to budget/politics.

Current status & recommended AE playbook:
- Status: Stalled / leaning lost. Procurement stage but likely lost to FastServe.ai or internal budget freeze.
- Short term next step: Offer a 2-week targeted follow-up POC that demonstrates burst protections (warm-standby + admission control) on a capped budget with explicit success criteria (p95 < 300ms under 6x bursts). Attach a smaller commitment option (3-month trial pricing).
- If no response in 7 business days, mark as closed-lost, reason: technical fit (burst capacity) + competitive pricing.

Relevant links: pricing deck, security FAQ, POC load test logs in drive. GMail thread contains procurement questions. Jira INF-6829 tracks KV cache investigation.

AE notes (Aisha): "They love the observability in Console — token-level cost breakdown sells. But until we show predictable burst behavior without a large commit, they won't push procurement. Competitor promising edge autoscale hurts our head-to-head."
